config.title: Controlled DatePicker

intro.title: Controlled DatePicker
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a controlled DatePicker component in Vue. You will learn how to manage a selected date using Vue's reactive state and how to update it based on user input. The core concept is controlling a component's state through props and events, ensuring the parent component manages the data. You will use Vue's ref for state, v-model for two-way binding, and handle date selection with a custom event. This teaches you how to create reusable, predictable form components in Vue.
intro.usecase: Controlled date pickers are essential in any form where users need to input or schedule dates, such as booking flights on travel websites, setting appointments in healthcare applications, or selecting delivery dates in e-commerce checkouts. They are also critical in data dashboards and reporting tools, allowing users to filter analytics by specific date ranges to view trends over time. As a developer, implementing a controlled date picker ensures the selected date is properly synchronized with your application's state, enabling validation, dynamic UI updates, and reliable data submission.

objectives: Initialize a reactive date state using Vue's ref() function
Bind the date state to a DatePicker component using v-model
Configure a DatePicker component with controlled properties and event handlers
Implement a handler function to update the date state when the user selects a date
Render the current selected date in the UI by accessing the reactive state
Manipulate the date state programmatically to reset or set default values
Integrate the controlled DatePicker within a form component while maintaining reactivity

steps.title: Import Vue and ref
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from 'vue' to set up reactive state for your DatePicker component.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.

// Importing Vue and ref for reactive state
import { ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports for Vue and ref are added at the top of the file.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to import Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the DatePicker component
steps.instruction: Define a Vue component named DatePicker that returns a simple div wrapper.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can create a component using a function that returns a template. Start with the component name and a function that returns a div element.
steps.seedCode:
import { ref } from 'vue';

// Define a Vue component named DatePicker here
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a DatePicker component function that returns a div element.
successCriteria: A DatePicker component is defined and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the DatePicker component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named DatePicker that returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a function named DatePicker that returns a div.

steps.title: Initialize selectedDate state
steps.instruction: Inside your DatePicker component, initialize a reactive state variable called selectedDate using ref, with an initial value of null.
steps.hint: Use the ref function you imported earlier to create a reactive reference. The syntax is: const selectedDate = ref(null);
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a reactive state variable
const count = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a reactive selectedDate variable initialized to null inside the component's setup function.
successCriteria: A const variable named selectedDate is declared and initialized with ref(null) inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using ref(null) to initialize the selectedDate variable inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The selectedDate state variable wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use ref(null) inside the setup function.

steps.title: Define handleDateChange handler
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named handleDateChange that takes a date parameter and updates selectedDate.value with that date.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives a date and assigns it to selectedDate.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a handleDateChange function that updates the selectedDate state when called with a new date.
successCriteria: The handleDateChange function is defined inside setup, takes a date parameter, and assigns it to selectedDate.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function takes a date parameter and updates selectedDate.value with it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handler isn't defined correctly. Create a function named handleDateChange that updates selectedDate.value with the date it receives.

steps.title: Add template structure with input
steps.instruction: Add a template section with an input element of type 'date' inside your DatePicker component.
steps.hint: In Vue components, you can add a template section using the template tag. Inside it, create an input element with type='date'.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a basic template structure with a date input element.
successCriteria: The component has a template section containing an input element with type='date'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both the template section and the input element with type='date'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure with date input wasn't added correctly. Check that you've included a template section with an input element of type 'date'.

steps.title: Bind selectedDate to input value
steps.instruction: In the template section, bind the input's v-model to selectedDate to connect the reactive state to the input.
steps.hint: Use v-model directive with the selectedDate reactive reference.
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element will be bound to the selectedDate reactive state via v-model.
successCriteria: The input element has v-model="selectedDate" attribute.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added v-model="selectedDate" to the input element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is not properly bound to the selectedDate state. Check that you've added v-model="selectedDate" to the input.

steps.title: Wire handleDateChange to input change
steps.instruction: Add the @input event listener to the date input element to call your handleDateChange handler.
steps.hint: Use @input to listen for changes on the input element and call handleDateChange with the event.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring an input event
<input type="text" @input="handleInput" />

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added @input="handleDateChange" to the date input element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element doesn't have the event listener wired correctly. Try adding @input="handleDateChange" to the input element.
